companies.subsequent_events: Q1 FY27 (Jun-Aug 2026, within period): completed $20B at-the-market common equity program (before commissions); debt fell ~$4.2B QoQ; equity rose to $67.2B. After 2026-08-31: Sep 10 results - RPO $664B (+$26B QoQ), >$30B new AI contracts mostly prepaid/bring-your-own-hardware; capex guide $90-95B unchanged; mgmt reiterates no additional debt issuance in calendar 2026 (FY27 financing plan ~$40B incl. the $20B ATM). ~Sep 24-25, 2026: force-majeure notice to Project Jupiter (NM) developer; ~$18B Jupiter construction loan quoted 89-91c. Late Sep 2026: Oracle 5y CDS at a record ~227 bp (TradingView/Seeking Alpha; vs ~144 bp at start of 2026 and ~203 bp in late July per Bloomberg-sourced reports). Oct 1, 2026: FT reports ~$7B 5-yr Tencent lease (unconfirmed). Sep 18, 2026: Fortune argues S&P's own metrics no longer support IG.
companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Senior unsecured IG notes; financial maintenance covenants not retrieved (historically none on Oracle notes - not re-verified). Policy commitments: 'strongly committed to maintaining an investment-grade credit rating as our top capital allocation priority'; Feb-2026 plan: ~$45-50B gross proceeds in CY2026, roughly half equity (MCP + up to $20B ATM) and half a single one-time IG bond issue, no further bonds in CY2026. S&P downgrade trigger adjusted leverage >4.5x (S&P forecast ~4.4x FY27-28 per secondary report). Bondholder class action filed Jan 2026 alleging concealment of debt needs. Lessor-borrowing guarantee up to $3.3B.
companies.credit_view: Oracle is the most stretched IG credit in the AI build-out: LTM FCF is roughly -$29B and FY27 gross capex of $90-95B against ~$34B of GAAP EBITDA means negative FCF persists through at least FY27, with S&P now at BBB- (one notch above HY) and Moody's Baa2 on negative outlook. Reported balance-sheet leverage looks moderate (~2.6x net, ~3.7x gross on GAAP EBITDA), but the real exposure is the $288B of signed-but-not-commenced leases (8x on-B/S lease liabilities) plus partner project debt (~$38B Vantage, ~$18B Jupiter) whose service depends on Oracle's rent. Mitigants: management has shifted funding to equity ($5B MCP + $20B ATM in 2026), customer prepayments/BYOH structures (net cash capex capped at $70B), and $37B of liquidity. The rating hinges on RPO conversion ($664B, roughly half OpenAI per S&P) - any OpenAI funding stress or site delay (Jupiter force majeure) would hit Oracle's lease obligations before its revenue, making a fall to HY at one agency the key tail risk.

companies.credit_view: SpaceX is currently a net-cash credit (~$100B cash/securities vs ~$38B debt at 6/30/26) anchored by Starlink (Q2 seg adj EBITDA $2.6B, 12M subs), which supports the BBB/Baa1/BBB+ ratings. The risk is the AI segment: capex is running ~$70B+ annualized (Q2 $18.4B, ~86% AI), so the IPO cash pile is being consumed quickly and management is already marketing another ~$40B of debt, which would push gross debt toward ~$80B. AI-segment revenue is concentrated in a few compute offtakes (notably Anthropic's terminable Colossus 1 lease), so leverage could re-rate fast if AI demand or pricing softens. Watch: cash burn vs. the remaining IPO proceeds, the structure of GPU-backed financing (secured/SPV vs. unsecured), and governance-driven rating caps.

companies.subsequent_events: Mar 31, 2026: closed $122B round at $852B post-money (SoftBank and a16z reported co-leads; Amazon, Nvidia, Microsoft, MGX, D.E. Shaw, TPG, T. Rowe participating). Reported investor amounts: Amazon $50B (of which ~$35B reportedly conditional on IPO/AGI - single low-authority source), Nvidia $30B, SoftBank $30B (secondary). Later 2026: reports of a new ~$30B round at ~$1.4T pre-money and IPO preparation.
companies.covenants_and_key_terms: None disclosed. Funding is equity-dependent; a meaningful share of the 2026 round is reportedly contingent (Amazon tranche) and SoftBank's share is itself debt-financed at SoftBank level.
companies.credit_view: OpenAI has no rated debt, but it is the single largest credit exposure in the AI build-out: ~$600-856B of compute commitments through 2030 (up to ~$1.4T over ~8 years on Altman's headline) against a ~$40B revenue run-rate is ~15-21x commitments-to-revenue (~35x on the $1.4T figure), with ~$278B of projected negative FCF through 2030 funded entirely by future equity raises. Its ability to pay depends on continuous access to private/IPO capital rather than operating cash flow. For counterparties this is the key wrong-way risk: Oracle (roughly half of its $664B RPO, plus $288B of uncommenced leases and partner project loans built for OpenAI), Microsoft ($250B Azure, but strong balance sheet and equity stake), CoreWeave (highly levered, contracts backstop its secured debt) and AWS ($38B, de minimis to Amazon). Any funding-round failure or contract renegotiation would transmit first to Oracle and CoreWeave credit spreads.

companies.other_off_bs_commitments: Disclosed compute commitments (company announcements): AWS - 'more than $100 billion' over ten years for up to 5 GW of Trainium2-4 capacity (Apr 20, 2026); Google + Broadcom - 5 GW of next-generation TPU capacity from 2027 ($ undisclosed; Apr 6 / May 28, 2026); Google Cloud - up to 1M TPUs, 'tens of billions of dollars', well over 1 GW, online 2026 (Oct 23, 2025); Microsoft Azure - $30B compute purchase commitment, up to 1 GW on NVIDIA systems (Nov 18, 2025); Fluidstack - $50B US data centers in Texas and New York, sites online through 2026 (Nov 12, 2025); SpaceX/xAI - all of Colossus 1 (>300 MW, >220k NVIDIA GPUs) (May 6, 2026), reportedly $1.25B/month (~$15B/yr) terminable on 90 days' notice. DERIVED floor of quantified $ commitments: >= ~$195B ($100B + $30B + $50B + ~$15B/yr Colossus) plus 'tens of billions' (Google 2025) plus undisclosed 5 GW Google/Broadcom; capacity ~12+ GW. Task-brief figure of ~$500B+ / ~15 GW not verified this session (plausible once Google/Broadcom 5 GW is priced).
companies.ltm_ebitda_basis: N/A. ltm_revenue field holds ANNUALIZED RUN-RATE REVENUE: 'crossed $47 billion' in May 2026 (company, Series H). Trajectory: ~$9B end-2025 -> $14B (Feb 12, 2026) -> >$30B (Apr 2026) -> >$47B (May 2026). No newer company figure found.
companies.ntm_ebitda_basis: N/A. Cash burn not found this session.
companies.subsequent_events: Feb 12, 2026: Series G $30B at $380B post-money (led by GIC and Coatue; includes part of Microsoft up to $5B / NVIDIA up to $10B commitments from Nov 2025). May 28, 2026: Series H $65B at $965B post-money (led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia). 2026 equity raised ~ $95B (derived). May 2026: Colossus 1 compute deal with SpaceX. No debt raise or credit facility disclosed in 2026 announcements.
companies.credit_view: Anthropic is the stronger of the two private AI-lab counterparties on revenue momentum (run-rate ~$9B to >$47B in five months) and liquidity (~$95B of equity raised in 2026), and quantifiable commitments (>= ~$195B, multi-year) are ~4x run-rate revenue (~10x if the reported ~$500B total is right) versus ~15-21x for OpenAI. Its compute is diversified across AWS, Google/Broadcom TPUs, Azure/NVIDIA, Fluidstack and SpaceX, so no single supplier is fully dependent on it, but the obligations are long-dated (AWS 10 years) while revenue is young and concentrated in API/enterprise usage. Counterparty read-through: low risk for AWS, Google and Microsoft (de minimis to their balance sheets); material for Fluidstack-linked developers (TeraWulf, Hut 8 and Google-backstopped leases), CoreWeave and SpaceX/xAI, whose site-level debt service relies on Anthropic offtake - note the Colossus 1 arrangement is reportedly terminable on 90 days' notice, making it weak collateral for SpaceX.
